deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a short administrative note at the top of an otherwise blank notebook page; the faint lines are show-through from the reverse side. The heading 'Verliehen:' means 'Lent out:'. It records items Hilbert had lent to others.

(1) Struck through: 'Liebmann, Göttinger Nachr. 1896'. This is probably an offprint or volume of the Göttinger Nachrichten, plausibly a note by Heinrich Liebmann, lent and later returned.

(2) Struck through: a second line whose reading is uncertain ('Engelhoff[?] Tannerd[?]' or similar); it is also a returned loan.

(3) 'Wilberts[?]/Hilberts[?] Bädeker in d. Nordseebäder'. This reads as a Baedeker travel guide to the North Sea resorts, lent to or belonging to the named person. After a comma comes 'Poincaré-Lindemann', almost certainly the German translation by F. and L. Lindemann of Poincaré's La science et l'hypothèse (Wissenschaft und Hypothese, Teubner 1904).

(4) 'Schwarzschild: " [ditto = Bädeker] Norwegen'. Karl Schwarzschild borrowed the Baedeker guide to Norway.

The diagonal blue-pencil strokes over the whole block probably mark the list as settled (items returned).

Schwarzschild was in Göttingen from 1901 to 1909 and the Lindemann translation dates from 1904. The note is therefore plausibly from c. 1904–1909. The 1896 entry is earlier; it may have been added to the list at an earlier stage.

Context: the previous page holds general mathematical-philosophical remarks (Klein; geometers vs. analysts; Jacobi, Weierstrass, Clebsch, Hesse). The next page lists recommended books (Weismann) and a series of numbers with dates, perhaps body weights.

results.what: Record of books and travel guides lent out (Baedeker guides; Poincaré's 'Wissenschaft und Hypothese' in Lindemann's translation; a Göttinger Nachrichten item of 1896)

deep.surprise_reason: A personal lending list with no mathematical content. The only minor biographical interest is that Schwarzschild borrowed a Baedeker for Norway and that Hilbert owned the Lindemann translation of Poincaré.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'Bücher' should read 'Bädeker' (Baedeker travel guide): 'Bädeker in d. Nordseebäder'. The preceding name may be 'Wilberts' rather than 'Hilberts' (initial letter uncertain).
Line 4: the ditto mark after 'Schwarzschild' stands under 'Bädeker', i.e. 'Schwarzschild: Bädeker Norwegen'.
'Poincaré-Lindemann' refers to the Lindemann translation of Poincaré's 'Wissenschaft und Hypothese' (1904).
Line 2 (struck through) is not reliably legible; 'Engelhoff Tannerd' is doubtful. The image is perhaps closer to 'Ehlerghess[?] Tannund[?]'.
The entire block is additionally cancelled with diagonal blue-pencil strokes, which the transcription does not note.
